takeaway: Melanocytes are found in the stratum basale, the deepest layer of the epidermis; the stratum corneum is the outermost keratin-filled layer.

question.text: With regard to the epidermis, in which layer are the melanin-producing melanocytes located?

lines.text: Here is the epidermis, drawn as a building with its layers.
At the very top is the stratum corneum, the outermost layer of keratin-filled cells with no nuclei.
Below it come the stratum granulosum and the stratum spinosum, both crossed out.
Right at the bottom, our little painter is the melanocyte, splashing melanin up toward the sun.
lines.say: (laugh) Right at the bottom, our little painter is the melanocyte, splashing melanin up toward the sun.

lines.text: He lives in the deepest layer, the stratum basale.
